Surgery Information.Surgery Findings: unremarkable, small amount of ascites in the pelvic region but washings were negative, small lesion in the liver was biopsied and recovered elements of a cyst

Surgery Information.Surgery Procedure: pylorus-preserving pancreatectomy with open cholecystectomy and portal vein and hepatic artery resection and interposition graft
Surgery Information.Surgery Location: pancreas, gallbladder, portal vein, hepatic artery
Surgery Information.Surgery Findings: 1.7 cm residual tumor mass within estimation of 51-90% of tumor cells destroyed, margins were negative, no positive lymph nodes

Additional Comments: The patient, a 63-year-old African American woman, initially presented with abdominal discomfort, bloating, and jaundice. Following the placement of a metal stent, she became relatively asymptomatic. Imaging revealed a mass in the head of the pancreas and a 2 cm adrenal mass, with the pancreatic mass being PET avid. An ultrasound showed a 3.2 cm fibroid in the uterus and thickened endometrium. EUS indicated encasement of the hepatic artery and invasion into the portal vein, and FNA confirmed adenocarcinoma. Post-laparoscopy, she developed pleuritic chest pain and shortness of breath, with CT showing interlobular septal thickening and ground glass opacities. She underwent a pylorus-preserving pancreatectomy with portal vein and hepatic artery resection, and pathology showed a 1.7 cm residual tumor with 51-90% tumor cell destruction and negative margins. Postoperatively, she experienced continued abdominal discomfort, particularly on the right side, and has lost 15 pounds since surgery.
